subject: math
title: Measure to the Nearest Half and Quarter Inch and Make Line Plots
seo_title: Grade 3 Line Plot Worksheets: Measure to the Nearest Half and Quarter Inch, Read and Make Line Plots
standard_text: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show the data by making a line plot, where the horizontal scale is marked off in appropriate units— whole numbers, halves, or quarters.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 line plot worksheets with pictures: measure to the nearest half and quarter inch with a ruler, read line plots, compare data and solve word problems. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Start at 0 and count spaces. Put one X above each length.
key_sub: Long marks are inches, middle marks are halves, short marks are quarters. On a line plot, each X is one measurement, and the tallest stack is the most common length.
body_html:
Measure with a ruler

Put the end of the object at 0. Look straight down from the other end and read the mark. A length is the number of spaces from 0, not the number of marks.

Halves and fourths of an inch

The marks on a ruler have different lengths. The longer the mark, the bigger the part it shows.

MarkWhat it showsExamples
Long mark with a numberWhole inches1, 2, 3
Middle markHalf inches12, 1 12, 2 12
Short markQuarter inches (fourths)14, 34, 2 14
Example

A ruler is marked in quarter inches. A nail ends 2 small spaces past 1. How long is it?

2 small spaces = 24 inch, which is the same as 12 inch. So the nail is 1 12 inches.

Answer: 1 12 inches

Make a line plot

A line plot shows many measurements at once. Draw a number line with marks that fit the data: whole numbers, halves or quarters. Then put one X above the mark for each measurement.

A class measured 10 leaves. The lengths in inches are: 2, 2 14, 2 14, 2 12, 2 12, 2 12, 2 34, 3, 3, 3 14.

Read a line plot

QuestionHow to find itAnswer
How many leaves are 2 12 inches long?Count the X's above 2 123
Which length is most common?Find the tallest stack2 12 in
How many leaves in all?1 + 2 + 3 + 1 + 2 + 110
How many more leaves are 2 12 inches than 2 inches?3 − 12
Example

How much longer is the longest leaf than the shortest leaf?

Longest: 3 14 in. Shortest: 2 in. Count up: from 2 to 3 is 1 inch, then from 3 to 3 14 is 14 inch more.

Answer: 1 14 inches

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Starting the object at the end of the ruler or at 1Line up the end of the object with 0
Counting tick marksCount the spaces between marks
Calling a short mark a halfMiddle marks are halves. Short marks are fourths
Reading the last number on the line plot as the longestThe longest is the X farthest to the right
Counting the X's in the column next to itPoint to the mark, then count straight up

faq.q: What is a line plot in 3rd grade math?
faq.a: A line plot is a number line with an X above it for each measurement. In 3rd grade, students measure lengths to the nearest half or quarter inch and show the data on a line plot.

faq.q: How do you measure to the nearest quarter inch?
faq.a: Line up the end of the object with 0. Each inch has 4 small spaces, each worth 1/4 inch. Read the whole inch, then count the small spaces past it, such as 2 and 3/4 inches.

faq.q: How do you make a line plot with fractions?
faq.a: Draw a number line marked in halves or fourths so every measurement has a mark. Then put one X above the mark for each measurement, stacking the X's when lengths repeat.

faq.q: Which marks on a ruler show half and quarter inches?
faq.a: The long numbered marks are whole inches. The middle mark between two numbers is the half inch, and the shortest marks are the quarter inches.

sets.title: Compare data on a line plot

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured some twigs. The line plot shows the lengths. How many more twigs are 5 inches long than 6 inches long?
items.e: 5 has 4 X's. 6 has 1 X. 4 − 1 = 3 more.

items.q: Mrs. Green's class measured some shells. The line plot shows the lengths. How many shells are longer than 1 12 inches?
items.e: Longer means to the right of 1 12. Do not count the X's above 1 12 itself. Add the X's to the right: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6.

items.q: Ms. Lee's class measured some leaves. The line plot shows the lengths. How many leaves are either 2 12 inches or 3 inches long?
items.e: Count the X's above 2 12: 2. Count the X's above 3: 4. Add them: 2 + 4 = 6.

items.q: Ms. Brown's class measured some ribbon pieces. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest ribbon piece than the shortest ribbon piece?
items.e: Longest: 2 34 inches. Shortest: 1 14 inches. Count up from the shortest: from 1 14 to 2 14 is 1 inch, then from 2 14 to 2 34 is 12 inch more. The difference is 1 12 inches.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured some pine cones. The line plot shows the lengths. How many more pine cones are 2 12 inches long than 4 inches long?
items.e: 2 12 has 3 X's. 4 has 1 X. 3 − 1 = 2 more.

items.q: Kai measured some caterpillars. The line plot shows the lengths. How many more caterpillars are 2 14 inches long than 1 12 inches long?
items.e: 2 14 has 5 X's. 1 12 has 2 X's. 5 − 2 = 3 more.

items.q: Mr. Kim's class measured some crayons. The line plot shows the lengths. How many crayons are either 2 inches or 2 34 inches long?
items.e: Count the X's above 2: 3. Count the X's above 2 34: 2. Add them: 3 + 2 = 5.

sets.title: Word problems: make and use line plots

items.q: Noah measured 11 earthworms. The lengths in inches are: 2 12, 3 12, 4, 3, 3 12, 4 12, 3 12, 4, 4 12, 3, 3 12. He made this line plot but forgot one X. Where does the missing X go?
items.e: Count how many times each length is in the list. 2 12 is in the list once, but the plot has no X above it. The missing X goes above 2 12.

items.q: Grace measured 10 crayons. The lengths in inches are: 2 14, 2 12, 2 34, 2 14, 2 12, 3 14, 3 14, 2 12, 3, 2 34. She made this line plot but forgot one X. Where does the missing X go?
items.e: Count how many times each length is in the list. 3 is in the list once, but the plot has no X above it. The missing X goes above 3.

items.q: Owen measured 10 rocks. The lengths in inches are: 1 12, 2 14, 2, 1 34, 1 12, 1 14, 2 14, 1 34, 1 14, 1 12. He made this line plot but forgot one X. Where does the missing X go?

items.q: Emma measured 11 feathers. The lengths in inches are: 3 12, 4, 3 12, 2, 3 12, 3 12, 3, 2 12, 4, 3, 3. She made this line plot but forgot one X. Where does the missing X go?

items.q: Leo made this line plot of pencil lengths. Then he measured one more pencil. It is 5 12 inches long. How many X's will be above 5 12 now?
items.e: There are 2 X's above 5 12 now. Add 1 X for the new pencil: 2 + 1 = 3.

items.q: Ava measured 8 crayons. The lengths in inches are: 1 12, 1 34, 2 14, 1 12, 2 12, 1 34, 2 34, 2 14. Which scale on the line plot has a mark for every length?
items.e: Some lengths, like 1 34 and 2 34, end in fourths. A line plot needs a mark for each one, so the number line must be marked in quarter inches.

items.q: Jack measured 4 shells: 2 12, 3, 2 34 and 4 inches. He makes a line plot marked in half inches: 2, 2 12, 3, 3 12, 4. Which length has no mark on this line plot?
items.e: Half-inch marks are whole numbers and halves. 2 34 ends in a fourth, so it falls between 2 12 and 3. It needs a line plot marked in quarter inches.

items.q: Sam measured 8 crayons. The lengths in inches are: 2 12, 2 12, 2 14, 2 12, 2 34, 2 12, 2 34, 2. How much longer is the longest crayon than the shortest crayon?
items.e: Find the longest, 2 34 inches, and the shortest, 2 inches. Do not just use the first and last numbers in the list. Count up from the shortest: from 2 to 2 34 is 34 inch. The difference is 34 inch.

items.q: Zoe measured 10 feathers. The lengths in inches are: 4 14, 4 12, 3 12, 3 12, 3 34, 3 12, 3 34, 3 34, 4, 3 12. How much longer is the longest feather than the shortest feather?
items.e: Find the longest, 4 12 inches, and the shortest, 3 12 inches. Do not just use the first and last numbers in the list. Count up from the shortest: from 3 12 to 4 12 is 1 inch. The difference is 1 inch.
